dossier.claim: Several passages alter how Saber’s competence, constraints, and relationship with Shirou are expressed: her advantage over Archer is reversed, uncertainty about Zouken’s authority becomes a presumed relationship, and explicit personal costs or reciprocal obligations are reduced. These local changes do not establish a general loss of her knightly independence.
dossier.sourcePattern: The Japanese distinguishes Saber’s own qualified combat assessment from Shirou’s incomplete knowledge of her allegiance. Physical staggering briefly prevents pursuit, and Shirou understands her cooperation to have cost her life. His welcome dinner separately acknowledges gratitude for the previous night.
dossier.englishEffect: The English reverses the combat comparison and changes whether into how for the possible relationship with Zouken. Elsewhere it replaces staggering with planted feet and omits the death and dinner-thanks clauses. These changes affect specific accounts of competence, imposed limits, and reciprocity; they do not all push Saber toward the same characterization.
dossier.limits: The English still preserves Saber's knightly refusal to harm unarmed innocents, her insistence on protecting and training Shirou, her distinction between calibrated strength and mercy, her effortless attack on Archer, and her direct declaration of love. These passages do not establish her ultimate fate, actual allegiance to Zouken, or a broad shift toward obedience. The dinner example concerns Shirou's acknowledgment of her, and the Rider example concerns a brief physical constraint. Her refusal to violate her beliefs and the Command Spell required to compel her also remain explicit; compressing the intrusion metaphor is not counted as a separate error.
dossier.diagnostic: 529 findings in this category; 5 cited passages.

findings.description: Rider's injuries inflicted by Saber become Saber's injuries healing.
findings.sourceReading: Rider spends resources on natural healing of body wounded by Saber.
findings.explanation: Rider's injuries inflicted by Saber become Saber's injuries healing.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十六日目-01:page4:1
contexts.japanese: セイバーによって傷つけられた体を癒す自然治癒。
contexts.english: Any of Saber's injuries are automatically healed.

findings.description: Offense preventing Saber attack becomes Saber stopping Rider with attacks.
findings.sourceReading: Rider keeps attacking in order to prevent Saber taking initiative; if Saber attacks both Rider and boy die immediately.
findings.explanation: Offense preventing Saber attack becomes Saber stopping Rider with attacks.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十六日目-01:page5:1
contexts.japanese: ライダーは攻め続ける事で、セイバーの攻撃を防いでいる。
contexts.english: Rider keeps attacking, while Saber stops her with attacks of her own.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十六日目-01:page5:1
contexts.japanese: セイバーが攻撃に転ずれば、自分はおろか主である少年まで瞬殺されるだろう。
contexts.english: Rider knows that she and the boy she calls Master will be killed instantly if Saber goes on the offense.

findings.description: Potential centimeters to heart become enacted thrust depth.
findings.sourceReading: Blade at his back needs only a further push of a few centimeters to pierce heart.
findings.explanation: Potential centimeters to heart become enacted thrust depth.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十六日目-02:page11:1
contexts.japanese: わずか数センチ、一押しするだけで心臓を穿つ、冷酷な死の重み。
contexts.english: The cold weight of death pushes in only a few centimeters, stopping just short of my heart.

findings.description: Saber's involuntary staggering becomes a planted stance. The resulting opening for Rider remains, but its physical cause changes.
findings.sourceReading: Saber staggers after deflecting the sword and cannot pursue Rider, creating the two-second opening.
findings.explanation: Saber's involuntary staggering becomes a planted stance. The resulting opening for Rider remains, but its physical cause changes.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十六日目-03:page8:1
contexts.japanese: 放たれた螺旋の剣を弾いたセイバーは、ライダーを追えずにたたらを踏んでいる。
contexts.english: Saber repels my loosed spiral sword and plants her feet instead of pursuing Rider.

findings.description: Petals shattered by black light become petals scattering black light.
findings.sourceReading: Four wings/petals have been shattered by black aurora and scatter as the chamber fills white.
findings.explanation: Petals shattered by black light become petals scattering black light.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十六日目-03:page27:1
contexts.japanese: 黒い極光に打ち砕かれた四枚羽を撒き散らしながら、
contexts.english: Four petals scatter the black light,

findings.description: Broken shield petals become black-light-scattering petals in other branch.
findings.sourceReading: Four petals broken by black aurora scatter before white light wins.
findings.explanation: Broken shield petals become black-light-scattering petals in other branch.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十六日目-04:page24:1
contexts.japanese: 黒い極光に打ち砕かれた四枚羽を撒き散らしながら、
contexts.english: Four petals scatter the black light,

findings.description: Ninety-percent cancellation line absent from chain-opening English.
findings.sourceReading: Japanese says Saber's holy sword cancels nine tenths of Bellerophon's light.
findings.explanation: Ninety-percent cancellation line absent from chain-opening English.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十六日目-04:page27:1
contexts.japanese: ベルレフォーンの光はその九割を、セイバーの聖剣によって相殺された。

findings.description: Only eight days becomes fewer than eight days.
findings.sourceReading: まだ八日しか is only eight elapsed days; the next self-correction says already eight.
findings.explanation: Only eight days becomes fewer than eight days.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十六日目-07:page2:1
contexts.japanese: 彼女を失ったあの夜から、まだ八日しか経っていない。
contexts.english: Less than eight days have passed since the night I lost her.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十六日目-07:page2:1
contexts.japanese: ……いや、もう八日と言うべきか。
contexts.english: ...No, I guess it's already been that long.

findings.description: Absolute killing intent omitted from first sight of Saber.
findings.sourceReading: Saber waits clothed in absolute killing intent.
findings.explanation: Absolute killing intent omitted from first sight of Saber.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十六日目-15:page2:1
contexts.japanese: 絶対の殺気を纏って、セイバーが待っていた。
contexts.english: stands Saber, waiting for us.

findings.description: Three intruders become both.
findings.sourceReading: Saber could face all three: Rin, Shirou and Rider, alone.
findings.explanation: Three intruders become both.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十六日目-15:page5:1
contexts.japanese: 桜を守る最強のサーヴァントであるセイバーなら、一人きりで俺たち三人の相手が出来る。
contexts.english: She's the strongest Servant protecting Sakura, and she could take us both alone.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十六日目-15:page26:1
contexts.japanese: 「士郎、貴方は後ろに。指示通り、セイバーの相手は私がします」
contexts.english: "Shirou, get behind me. I will engage Saber, as planned."

findings.description: Remaining Shirou and Rider become Shirou alone.
findings.sourceReading: After Rin goes on, boy and Rider remain.
findings.explanation: Remaining Shirou and Rider become Shirou alone.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十六日目-15:page19:1
contexts.japanese: 遠坂が奥に進み、残されたのは俺とライダーだけだ。
contexts.english: Tohsaka's gone, leaving only me.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十六日目-15:page20:1
contexts.japanese: 「殺す、とは聞き捨てなりませんね。貴方が手にかけるのはこの道を通る者のみ。彼がこの場に留まるのなら、貴方に襲われる事はない筈ですが」
contexts.english: "Did I hear you correctly? You said that you would only kill those who attempt to pass. If he stays here, you should not attack him."

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十六日目-15:page21:1
contexts.japanese: 違いますか、ライダー」
contexts.english: Am I wrong, Rider?"

findings.description: Grinding teeth at resemblance becomes suppressing the words.
findings.sourceReading: Sakura grinds her teeth thinking it is like Excalibur's very light.
findings.explanation: Grinding teeth at resemblance becomes suppressing the words.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十六日目-17:page14:1
contexts.japanese: セイバーの宝具、エクスカリバーの光そのものではないか、と少女は歯を軋ませる。
contexts.english: She stops herself from saying that it's almost exactly like Saber's Excalibur.

findings.description: Weilding is misspelled.
findings.sourceReading: Knight of sword emerges dark/tainted; English's intended participle is wielding.
findings.explanation: Weilding is misspelled.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十四日目-06:page22:1
contexts.japanese: 黒く汚染された剣の騎士が這い上がる。
contexts.english: A knight weilding a dark, tainted sword emerges.

findings.description: Shirou's stated atonement for Saber's death becomes repayment for her cooperation. 'Also' becomes 'the only way,' changing both the expressed cost of following him and his reason for continuing.
findings.sourceReading: Continuing the fight is also atonement toward Saber, whom Shirou understands to have died after going along with his selfishness.
findings.explanation: Shirou's stated atonement for Saber's death becomes repayment for her cooperation. 'Also' becomes 'the only way,' changing both the expressed cost of following him and his reason for continuing.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十日目-04:page23:1
contexts.japanese: ……それが俺の我が侭につき合い、命を落としたセイバーへの償いでもある。
contexts.english: ...It's the only way I can repay Saber for going along with my selfishness.

findings.description: The swordsman's cut through Berserker's unguarded body disappears.
findings.sourceReading: Black armor passes through greatsword and debris, then flashes a cut across the exposed body.
findings.explanation: The swordsman's cut through Berserker's unguarded body disappears.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十日目-11:page8:1
contexts.japanese: 吹き荒ぶ風の元凶はあの黒い剣士なのか、黒い甲冑はバーサーカーの大剣と土塊をすり抜け、無防備な体を一閃する。
contexts.english: The black-armored Servant breezes past Berserker's greatsword and earthen assault, as if it's the source of this raging wind.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十日目-11:page9:1
contexts.japanese: それを、黒い剣士は苦もなく切断する。
contexts.english: And the black swordsman easily slices it open.

findings.description: A darkness-swallowing-light simile becomes inky light threatening to swallow Berserker whole.
findings.sourceReading: The sword paints Berserker's flank black like light swallowed by lightless darkness.
findings.explanation: A darkness-swallowing-light simile becomes inky light threatening to swallow Berserker whole.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十日目-11:page9:1
contexts.japanese: 無明の闇が光を呑むように、剣はバーサーカーの横腹を黒で塗りつぶしていった。
contexts.english: A sword paints Berserker's flank in black, the inky light threatening to swallow him whole.

findings.description: Many Noble Phantasms exceeding the sword in craftsmanship becomes few being able to rival it.
findings.sourceReading: Numerous Noble Phantasms surpass the sword in fine modeling and skilled ironwork; its superiority lies elsewhere.
findings.explanation: Many Noble Phantasms exceeding the sword in craftsmanship becomes few being able to rival it.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十日目-19:page8:1
contexts.japanese: 造型の細やかさ、鍛え上げられた鉄の巧みさで言えば、上回る宝具は数あろう。
contexts.english: Few Noble Phantasms can rival its elegant design and fine worksmanship.

findings.description: A sword outside nonhuman craft becomes not a work of mankind.
findings.sourceReading: The sword relies neither on myth nor on inhuman/nonhuman art; it is forged from human thought alone.
findings.explanation: A sword outside nonhuman craft becomes not a work of mankind.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十日目-19:page9:1
contexts.japanese: 神話に寄らず、人ならざる業にも属さず、ただ想いだけで鍛え上げられた結晶だからこそ—あの剣は空想の身で、最強の座に在り続ける。
contexts.english: Neither a relic of myth nor a work of mankind, it is a crystallization crafted from our feelings alone—a sword of pure fantasy, sitting at the apex.

findings.description: The explanation of Illya's fear loses the immediate threat to her own life. It describes her witnessing Berserker's death instead of facing both his defeat and approaching death herself.
findings.sourceReading: Illya faces both her Servant's defeat and death immediately threatening her.
findings.explanation: The explanation of Illya's fear loses the immediate threat to her own life. It describes her witnessing Berserker's death instead of facing both his defeat and approaching death herself.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十日目-19:page16:1
contexts.japanese: 自らのサーヴァントの敗北と、目前に迫った死。
contexts.english: Illya just watched her Servant die in battle.

findings.description: A broken helm implying prior head injury becomes an opportunity to inflict head damage.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou infers that because the helm was broken, Saber must already have sustained some damage to the head, and chooses that point.
findings.explanation: A broken helm implying prior head injury becomes an opportunity to inflict head damage.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十日目-19:page29:1
contexts.japanese: 兜を砕かれた、という事は頭部になんらかのダメージを負っている筈だ。
contexts.english: Now that her helmet is broken, I should be able to do some damage if I go for the head.

findings.description: A precise absolute image of surviving and defeating Saber becomes generic full commitment.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou believes he cannot even contest Saber unless he fights under an absolute image in which he himself survives and defeats the enemy.
findings.explanation: A precise absolute image of surviving and defeating Saber becomes generic full commitment.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十日目-19:page29:1
contexts.japanese: その、絶対のイメージの下で斬り合わなければ、セイバーとは勝負にもなり得ない—！
contexts.english: Unless I imagine myself fully committing to this, I don't have a chance against her...!

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十日目-19:page29:1
contexts.japanese: 自分は生き延びて敵を倒す。
contexts.english: I'll defeat my enemy and survive.

findings.description: A slash sharp enough to reap rice stalks becomes one precise enough to cut a grain of rice.
findings.sourceReading: The blade sweeps Shirou's exposed neck with the sharpness used to reap ears/stalks of rice.
findings.explanation: A slash sharp enough to reap rice stalks becomes one precise enough to cut a grain of rice.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十日目-19:page31:1
contexts.japanese: 稲穂を刈る鋭さで、衛宮士郎の無防備な首を薙ぎ払う。
contexts.english: It's a slash precise enough to cut a grain of rice, coming for Shirou Emiya's head.

findings.description: Saber's blade stopping at a single layer of skin becomes stopping shy of the neck.
findings.sourceReading: The sword has reached Shirou and stops at the thin skin of his neck, leaving his head attached.
findings.explanation: Saber's blade stopping at a single layer of skin becomes stopping shy of the neck.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十日目-19:page32:1
contexts.japanese: セイバーの剣は、俺の薄皮一枚で止まっている。
contexts.english: Saber's sword stops just shy of my neck.

findings.description: The English treats Saber becoming Zouken's Servant as established and leaves only the mechanism unknown. The Japanese leaves the relationship itself uncertain.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou does not know whether Saber has become Zouken's Servant; only her hostility is established.
findings.explanation: The English treats Saber becoming Zouken's Servant as established and leaves only the mechanism unknown. The Japanese leaves the relationship itself uncertain.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十日目-24:page6:1
contexts.japanese: あの“黒い影”がなんなのか、セイバーが臓硯のサーヴァントになったのかも判らない。
contexts.english: I have no idea what that black Shadow is, nor how Saber became Zouken's Servant.

findings.description: The refusal branch repeats the presupposition that Saber became Zouken's Servant.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou does not know whether Saber entered a contract with Zouken.
findings.explanation: The refusal branch repeats the presupposition that Saber became Zouken's Servant.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート十日目-25:page3:1
contexts.japanese: あの“黒い影”がなんなのか、セイバーが臓硯のサーヴァントになったのかも判らない。
contexts.english: I have no idea what that black Shadow is, nor how Saber became Zouken's Servant.

findings.description: Saber and Kiritsugu surviving to the end becomes winning the war.
findings.sourceReading: Saber says she cooperated with Kiritsugu and remained/won through to the final stage of the previous war.
findings.explanation: Saber and Kiritsugu surviving to the end becomes winning the war.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート四日目-01:page20:1
contexts.japanese: 前回の聖杯戦争のおり、衛宮切嗣はマスターの一人でした。私は彼と協力して聖杯戦争に挑み、最後まで勝ち残りました。
contexts.english: Kiritsugu Emiya was one of the Masters in the last Holy Grail War. I fought alongside him for the Grail, and we won.

findings.description: The victim not surviving if they remain still becomes doubt that the pair can help.
findings.sourceReading: Saber says that if things continue this way, the attacked person will not be saved, despite not knowing what happened.
findings.explanation: The victim not surviving if they remain still becomes doubt that the pair can help.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート四日目-03:page7:1
contexts.japanese: 「悲鳴が止みました。感じ取れる気配も消えかけています。何が起きたかは判りませんが、このままでは襲われた者は助からないでしょう」
contexts.english: "The scream stopped. The presence we sensed is fading. I don't know what just happened, but I doubt we'll be able to help whoever was attacked."

findings.description: Shirou's skill failing to match his plan becomes a shared failure to account for his skill.
findings.sourceReading: Saber says Shirou's action itself was right; if there was a shortcoming, only his ability failed to keep pace with his idea.
findings.explanation: Shirou's skill failing to match his plan becomes a shared failure to account for his skill.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート四日目-04:page6:1
contexts.japanese: 「いえ、マスターの行動自体は正しい。失点があるとしたら、シロウの技量が考えに付いてこなかっただけでしょう。
contexts.english: "No, Master, your actions were correct. If a mistake was made, it was that we failed to account for your skill level.

findings.description: A slow, lumbering target becomes a cautious target.
findings.sourceReading: Rider presses the attack as if cornering slow and heavy prey.
findings.explanation: A slow, lumbering target becomes a cautious target.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート四日目-05:page21:1
contexts.japanese: 敵は長い髪をなびかせ、鈍重な獲物を追い詰めるように畳み掛けてくる。
contexts.english: The enemy's long hair whips through the air, hounding her cautious prey.

findings.description: Sensing something ominous becomes being repulsed.
findings.sourceReading: Saber backs away slightly, apparently sensing something sinister or ill-omened in Zouken.
findings.explanation: Sensing something ominous becomes being repulsed.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート四日目-05:page49:1
contexts.japanese: ……老人に不吉なものを感じたのか、セイバーはかすかに後じさる。
contexts.english: Saber shifts slightly backward, as if repulsed by him.

findings.description: Uncertainty whether even one comparable Servant appeared becomes a recalled definite example.
findings.sourceReading: Zouken judges that perhaps not even one Servant of Saber's caliber appeared in past wars.
findings.explanation: Uncertainty whether even one comparable Servant appeared becomes a recalled definite example.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート四日目-05:page50:1
contexts.japanese: 「……ふむ。なるほど、これではライダーが敗れるのも道理。さぞ名のある英霊とお見受けした。これほどのサーヴァント、過去の戦いにおいても一人現れたかどうか」
contexts.english: "...Hm, I see. It's little wonder Rider lost. You are a Heroic Spirit of some renown. I seem to recall a Servant as powerful as this in one of the past wars."

findings.description: Saber's decision not to pursue Shinji gains a for-my-sake motive.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou supposes she judged there was no need to pursue Shinji now that he was no longer a Master.
findings.explanation: Saber's decision not to pursue Shinji gains a for-my-sake motive.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート四日目-05:page54:1
contexts.japanese: マスターでなくなった慎二を追う必要はない、と考えてくれたのだろう。
contexts.english: She's probably decided—for my sake—that Shinji isn't worth pursuing now that he's no longer a Master.

findings.description: An already concluded defeat becomes an intended withdrawal.
findings.sourceReading: Zouken says Shinji has lost and Matou's participation in this war has consequently ended early, then asks whether Saber will still cut him down.
findings.explanation: An already concluded defeat becomes an intended withdrawal.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート四日目-05:page83:1
contexts.japanese: 「ともあれ、慎二は敗れた。此度の戦いは早々に我らの敗退となったが—それでもこの老体を斬るかね、セイバーのサーヴァントよ」
contexts.english: "In any case, Shinji has lost. We intend to withdraw early from the war this time...but you would still cut this old man down, Saber?"

findings.description: Shirou starting to run after handing over the woman becomes Saber starting to run.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou entrusts the woman to Saber and sets off running; she then announces she will lead and moves ahead.
findings.explanation: Shirou starting to run after handing over the woman becomes Saber starting to run.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート四日目-05:page88:1
contexts.japanese: 女性をセイバーに預けて走り出す。
contexts.english: Saber takes the woman and starts running.

findings.description: A little carelessness causing a repeat becomes Shirou recklessly repeating the event.
findings.sourceReading: Saber warns that even slight carelessness could cause last night's near-fatal situation to recur.
findings.explanation: A little carelessness causing a repeat becomes Shirou recklessly repeating the event.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート四日目-07:page5:1
contexts.japanese: 「それで、何をされたのですかシロウ……！　貴方の傷はまだ完治してはいない。少しの油断で昨夜の繰り返しになるのだと、貴方自身も判っている筈です……！」
contexts.english: "What did he do to you, Shirou!? Your wounds aren't fully healed yet. You know what will happen if you're reckless enough to repeat what happened last night!"

findings.description: Shirou's cheeks loosening into a smile becomes his cheeks burning.
findings.sourceReading: Saber's indignant face is so fresh to Shirou that his expression involuntarily softens into another smile.
findings.explanation: Shirou's cheeks loosening into a smile becomes his cheeks burning.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート四日目-07:page9:1
contexts.japanese: そう抗議する顔すら新鮮で、つい頬が緩んでしまう。
contexts.english: Even her indignation is amusing, and my cheeks start burning.

findings.description: Saber jumping backward becomes flinching and taking one step.
findings.sourceReading: She springs backward with a sustained shuffling sound after Shirou calls her properly a girl.
findings.explanation: Saber jumping backward becomes flinching and taking one step.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート四日目-07:page15:1
contexts.japanese: ざざ、と後ろに跳び退くセイバー。
contexts.english: Saber flinches and takes a step back.

findings.description: Softhearted goodness becomes meddling.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou wonders whether Saber is an お人好し—a kind, overly good-natured person—or a perfectionist.
findings.explanation: Softhearted goodness becomes meddling.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート四日目-07:page20:1
contexts.japanese: 「—お人好しなんだか、完璧主義なんだかな」
contexts.english: "I can't tell if you're a busybody or a perfectionist."

findings.description: Fulfilling an overdue promise becomes doing a promise.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou thinks he must now properly fulfill the promise that should have been exchanged at the beginning.
findings.explanation: Fulfilling an overdue promise becomes doing a promise.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート四日目-07:page24:1
contexts.japanese: 交わすべきだった約束を、ここできちんと果たさないと。
contexts.english: I have to make her a promise that I should have done from the beginning.

findings.description: A patrol that amounts to relying on chance becomes an idea that happened to seem good to Shirou.
findings.sourceReading: Patrolling on foot is like hoping for coincidence, although Saber calls the method dangerous but reliable.
findings.explanation: A patrol that amounts to relying on chance becomes an idea that happened to seem good to Shirou.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート四日目-08:page2:1
contexts.japanese: 偶然に期待するようなものだが、セイバー曰く『危険ではあるが確実』な手なのだそうだ。
contexts.english: It just happened to seem like a good idea to me, but Saber said that it was a "risky but certain" choice.

findings.description: No mana supply becomes no extra mana.
findings.sourceReading: Saber receives no magical energy from Shirou and must spend her own reserves merely maintaining existence.
findings.explanation: No mana supply becomes no extra mana.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート四日目-08:page18:1
contexts.japanese: 俺からの魔力提供がないセイバーは、それこそ日々『ここにいる』だけで精一杯なのだ。
contexts.english: Without any extra magical energy from me, it takes all of Saber's power just to exist.

findings.description: Shirou's wish to make up for a leftovers lunch becomes an offer based on having leftovers available, changing why he insists on dinner.
findings.sourceReading: Because lunch was only leftovers, Shirou urges Saber to eat a proper evening meal before sleeping.
findings.explanation: Shirou's wish to make up for a leftovers lunch becomes an offer based on having leftovers available, changing why he insists on dinner.

contexts.ref: 桜ルート四日目-08:page24:1
contexts.japanese: 「魔力の温存は判ったよ。けど人間食事も大切だろ。昼は余りもので済ませちまったから、夕飯はちゃんと食べてくれ。寝るのはその後でいいじゃないか」
contexts.english: "I know you need to save energy, but meals are important, too. I still have some leftovers from lunch, so let me fix you dinner. You can go to bed after that."

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page55:1
contexts.japanese: しばらくは立ち直れないだろうなって思ってたのよ」
contexts.english: I was worried it would take a while for you to recover from all this."

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page56:1
contexts.japanese: それは、もういない彼女の事だった。
contexts.english: She's talking about...the girl who's not with me now.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page56:1
contexts.japanese: あれから二ヶ月—それだけの月日が経って初めて口にした、金の髪をした少女の話。
contexts.english: It's been two months, and this is the first time we've brought up the golden-haired girl.

counterexamples.description: Shirou's apparent next-day normality alarms Rin rather than reassuring her.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She fears abrupt death despite his composed surface.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's apparent next-day normality alarms Rin rather than reassuring her.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page57:1
contexts.japanese: 「—けどフタを開けてみれば、士郎ったら今まで通りだったでしょ。落ち込むどころの話じゃなくて、次の日にはもうケロリとしてた」
contexts.english: "But when it actually happened, you acted the same as always. You didn't seem depressed. You were even acting like nothing happened the next day."

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page58:1
contexts.japanese: 「……その時にね、こいつ大丈夫かなー、とも思ったのよ。うまく言えないんだけど、次の日にはあっさり事故で死んじゃうような雰囲気だった」
contexts.english: "That's when I started to get worried about whether you were really okay or not. I can't really explain it, but it felt like you were going to die in some freak accident the next day or something."

counterexamples.description: Shirou's lack of lingering regret remains qualified and calm rather than boastful.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He says probably and explicitly denies putting up a front.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's lack of lingering regret remains qualified and calm rather than boastful.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page66:1
contexts.japanese: 「じゃあもう未練はないんだ。セイバーが、いなくなってもさ」
contexts.english: "So you don't have any regrets? You know, about Saber being gone."

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page67:1
contexts.japanese: 「—ああ。未練なんて、きっと無い」
contexts.english: "Yeah...I don't have any regrets... Probably."

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page67:1
contexts.japanese: 強がりでもなく、自分でも驚くぐらい穏やかな心で告げた。
contexts.english: I'm not trying to put up a front. I even surprise myself with how at peace I sound.

counterexamples.description: No regret coexists with recognizing another possible choice and defending the beauty both protected.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou does not claim the relationship was painless or optimally resolved.
counterexamples.explanation: No regret coexists with recognizing another possible choice and defending the beauty both protected.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page68:1
contexts.japanese: 後悔なんてないし、言い残した事もなかった。
contexts.english: Nothing was left unsaid, so I don't regret anything.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page68:1
contexts.japanese: あの別れには、全てがあった。
contexts.english: Everything went into the moment we said goodbye.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page68:1
contexts.japanese: それは意地の張り合いで、本当はあいつの手を掴まえて、少女の夢を叶えるべきだったのかもしれない。
contexts.english: Maybe we were both stubborn, and maybe I really should have grabbed her hand and made her dream come true.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page69:1
contexts.japanese: それでも—お互いが美しいと感じたものがあって、それを必死に、最後まで守り通した。
contexts.english: But there was something we both felt was beautiful, and we both desperately tried to protect it until the very end.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page69:1
contexts.japanese: 悔いる事はない。
contexts.english: I have no regrets.

counterexamples.description: Shirou expects details to fade while preserving the fact that he loved Saber.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Continued love survives the claim of no regrets.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou expects details to fade while preserving the fact that he loved Saber.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page71:1
contexts.japanese: 「ああ。けど、今も夢に見る。これから先も、ずっとあいつの事を思い出すよ。
contexts.english: "Yeah. But I still dream about her. I'm going to remember her for the rest of my life.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page71:1
contexts.japanese: いつか記憶が薄れて、あいつの声もあいつの仕草も忘れていく。
contexts.english: One day, my memories of her will fade, and I'll forget her voice and her mannerisms.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page71:1
contexts.japanese: それでも—こんな事があったと、セイバーっていうヤツが好きだったって事だけは、ずっとずっと覚えてる」
contexts.english: But still...I'll never forget what happened, or that I loved her."

counterexamples.description: Rin gives no verbal answer but becomes visibly elated.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Her reaction remains narrated rather than explained as a confession.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin gives no verbal answer but becomes visibly elated.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page72:1
contexts.japanese: 遠坂は何も言わない。
contexts.english: Tohsaka doesn't say a thing.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page72:1
contexts.japanese: ただ、訳もなく上機嫌な体で、弾むような足取りをし始める。
contexts.english: But for some reason, she looks elated. She's practically skipping now.

counterexamples.description: The blue sky remains close-feeling but unreachable.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Physical distance and emotional proximity remain in tension.
counterexamples.explanation: The blue sky remains close-feeling but unreachable.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page78:1
contexts.japanese: —遠くには青い空。
contexts.english: The blue sky is off in the distance.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page78:1
contexts.japanese: こんなにも近くに感じるのに、
contexts.english: It feels so close...

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page78:1
contexts.japanese: 手を伸ばしても掴めない。
contexts.english: ...but even if I reached out, I could never grasp it.

counterexamples.description: Shared time can remain without a physical object, allowing Shirou to keep running.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Distance does not erase the belief in continuing connection.
counterexamples.explanation: Shared time can remain without a physical object, allowing Shirou to keep running.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page80:1
contexts.japanese: 手に残る物はないけれど、同じ時間にいて、同じ物を見上げた。
contexts.english: There may be nothing physical left, but we both shared time together and looked up at the same things.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page80:1
contexts.japanese: それを覚えているのなら—遠く離れていても、共に有ると信じられる。
contexts.english: If I can remember that...I can believe that we're still together, even across such a great distance.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page80:1
contexts.japanese: なくなる物があるように、なくならない物だってあると頷けるのだ。
contexts.english: Some things are bound to disappear, but others never will.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page81:1
contexts.japanese: だから、今は走り続ける。
contexts.english: So I'm going to keep running.

counterexamples.description: The narrative shifts from Shirou's present into the king's final battlefield.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The country-splitting battle ends in the king's victory.
counterexamples.explanation: The narrative shifts from Shirou's present into the king's final battlefield.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page83:1
contexts.japanese: —戦いは終わった。
contexts.english: The battle is over.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page83:1
contexts.japanese: 彼女の最後の戦場、国を二つに分けて行われた戦いは、王の勝利で幕を下ろした。
contexts.english: This is her final battlefield...the battle that split her country in half, and ended with the king's victory.

counterexamples.description: Bedivere, the wounded white horse and the king remain the surviving traveling group.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The king lies over the horse's back.
counterexamples.explanation: Bedivere, the wounded white horse and the king remain the surviving traveling group.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page85:1
contexts.japanese: 騎士の手には手綱が握られ、傷ついた白馬が懸命に付いていく。
contexts.english: He grips his horse's reins as the wounded white steed does its best to keep up.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page85:1
contexts.japanese: 生き残ったものは騎士と白馬。
contexts.english: The knight and the white horse are the only survivors.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page85:1
contexts.japanese: そして白馬の背に倒れ伏した、一人の王だけだった。
contexts.english: Draped over the horse's back is the wounded king.

counterexamples.description: The pre-reveal narration deliberately retains male pronouns for knight and king.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Retrospective knowledge does not rewrite the viewpoint before page111's correction.
counterexamples.explanation: The pre-reveal narration deliberately retains male pronouns for knight and king.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page86:1
contexts.japanese: 「王……！　アーサー王、こちらに—！」
contexts.english: "Your Majesty! King Arthur...this way!"

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page86:1
contexts.japanese: 自身も傷を負っているであろうに、騎士は全力で戦場を駆けていく。
contexts.english: The knight must be wounded himself, but he runs with all his might.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page86:1
contexts.japanese: 騎士が仕える王は、死に捕らわれていた。
contexts.english: The king he serves is on the verge of death.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page86:1
contexts.japanese: 敵軍の王を一騎打ちの末破ったものの、王自身も致命傷を負っていたのだ。
contexts.english: Even after defeating the rival king in single combat, his king sustained a fatal wound.

counterexamples.description: Bedivere's belief in the king's immortality remains tied to the sacred sword.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The narration initially entertains his sincere belief before correcting it.
counterexamples.explanation: Bedivere's belief in the king's immortality remains tied to the sacred sword.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page87:1
contexts.japanese: —或いは、騎士は真実思っていたのかもしれない。
contexts.english: Or perhaps the knight truly believes...

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page87:1
contexts.japanese: 彼らの王は不滅だと。
contexts.english: ...that his king is immortal.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page87:1
contexts.japanese: 聖剣の導きがある限り、王は決して滅びないと。
contexts.english: So long as they have the guidance of the sacred sword, the king will never perish.

counterexamples.description: Bedivere serves this king personally and rises to the personal guard hoping to see the hidden face.
counterexamples.sourceReading: His loyalty is not generic service to the country.
counterexamples.explanation: Bedivere serves this king personally and rises to the personal guard hoping to see the hidden face.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page90:1
contexts.japanese: 彼は国に仕えたのではない。
contexts.english: The knight did not serve his country.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page90:1
contexts.japanese: 彼はこの王だからこそ剣を預け、力になろうと邁進し、若輩の身でありながら王の近衛にまで上り詰めたのだ。
contexts.english: And that is why he entrusted his sword to his king, strove to aid his king, and rose to the position of the king's personal guard despite his young age.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page90:1
contexts.japanese: 或いは、身近にまで行けば、王の素顔が見られるのではと期待した。
contexts.english: Rather, he hoped that if he could someday get close enough, he could see his king's real face.

counterexamples.description: Close service disproves Bedivere's hope because the king never smiles.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Proximity and repeated observation do not grant the desired private face.
counterexamples.explanation: Close service disproves Bedivere's hope because the king never smiles.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page92:1
contexts.japanese: だが、その考えは間違っていた。
contexts.english: The knight was proved wrong, though.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page92:1
contexts.japanese: 他のどの騎士よりも身近に控え、その振る舞いを見続けてきた。
contexts.english: He guarded the king more closely than any knight, and always observed the king's behavior.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page92:1
contexts.japanese: だというのに、一度もなかった。
contexts.english: But the moment he wished for never came.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page92:1
contexts.japanese: 彼の王が笑った事など、ただの一度もなかったのだ。
contexts.english: His king never smiled.

counterexamples.description: The king's glory and total lack of ease fuel Bedivere's wish for reward.
counterexamples.sourceReading: His anger is protective rather than resentment of the king.
counterexamples.explanation: The king's glory and total lack of ease fuel Bedivere's wish for reward.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page93:1
contexts.japanese: これだけの偉業を成し遂げ、栄光の中にいる筈の王が。
contexts.english: The king should radiate glory, having achieved such success.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page93:1
contexts.japanese: その実、一時も安らかな顔を見せなかったのだ。
contexts.english: But never once did the king seem at ease, even for a moment.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page93:1
contexts.japanese: 許せなかった。
contexts.english: He couldn't stand it.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page93:1
contexts.japanese: だからこそ、いつか—この王のかんばせに、光が与えられる事を願ったのだ。
contexts.english: And so he wished for his king to be rewarded with light.

counterexamples.description: The unfulfilled wish for the king's peace drives Bedivere's refusal of death.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He thinks an ending here would leave the great king unrewarded.
counterexamples.explanation: The unfulfilled wish for the king's peace drives Bedivere's refusal of death.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page94:1
contexts.japanese: それはまだ成し得ていない。
contexts.english: That has yet to be accomplished.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page94:1
contexts.japanese: 王はまだ孤独のまま。
contexts.english: The king still remains solitary.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page94:1
contexts.japanese: 故に、騎士は王の死を拒み続けた。
contexts.english: And so the knight refuses to accept his king's death.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page94:1
contexts.japanese: それではあまりにも、この偉大な王が報われないではないか、と。
contexts.english: If it does, this great king will never be rewarded.

counterexamples.description: Bedivere places the king by a tree and faces a half-day ride to the harbor forces.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The logistics remain desperate and concrete.
counterexamples.explanation: Bedivere places the king by a tree and faces a half-day ride to the harbor forces.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page95:1
contexts.japanese: 「王、今はこちらに。すぐに兵を呼んでまいります」
contexts.english: "Your Majesty, please stay here. I will summon reinforcements right away."

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page95:1
contexts.japanese: 辿り着いた森で、騎士は王の体を大樹に預けた。
contexts.english: Once they reach the forest, the knight leans his king's body against a large tree.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page95:1
contexts.japanese: 事態は一刻を争う。
contexts.english: It is a race against time.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page95:1
contexts.japanese: 港に残してきた自軍まで、どれほど馬を速めようと半日。
contexts.english: Even riding hard on horseback, it will take half a day to bring back the troops they left at the harbor.

counterexamples.description: The supposedly unconscious king calls Bedivere by name and reports a dream.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The return of voice remains the knight's surprise.
counterexamples.explanation: The supposedly unconscious king calls Bedivere by name and reports a dream.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page96:1
contexts.japanese: 「—ベディヴィエール」
contexts.english: "...Bedivere."

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page96:1
contexts.japanese: その前に。
contexts.english: Before he can leave...

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page96:1
contexts.japanese: 意識のない筈の王が、騎士の名を口にした。
contexts.english: ...the king he thought unconscious calls out to him.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page97:1
contexts.japanese: 「王！？　意識が戻られましたか……！？」
contexts.english: "Your Majesty!? Have you woken up!?"

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page97:1
contexts.japanese: 「……うむ。少し、夢を見ていた」
contexts.english: "Yes... I was having a dream."

counterexamples.description: The king asks whether the same dream can continue after waking, and Bedivere knowingly prepares a lie.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The question concerns continuation, not a different dream.
counterexamples.explanation: The king asks whether the same dream can continue after waking, and Bedivere knowingly prepares a lie.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page100:1
contexts.japanese: 「—いや。そなたの言い分に驚いた。夢とは、目を覚ました後でも見れるものなのか。違う夢ではなく、目を瞑れば、また同じものが現れると……？」
contexts.english: "No, you only surprised me. Can you still dream after you've woken? Are you saying I will return to that same dream after I close my eyes?"

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page100:1
contexts.japanese: 今度は騎士が驚く番である。
contexts.english: Now it's the knight's turn to be surprised.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page100:1
contexts.japanese: 彼は言葉に詰まった後、それが偽りと知りながらも返答する。
contexts.english: For a moment, he is at a loss for words. At length, he responds, though he knows there is no truth to what he says.

counterexamples.description: Bedivere lies that strong desire can return someone to the same dream.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The narration immediately states that dreams are one-time and discontinuous.
counterexamples.explanation: Bedivere lies that strong desire can return someone to the same dream.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page101:1
contexts.japanese: 「—はい。強く思えば、同じ夢を見続ける事も出来るでしょう。私にも経験があります」
contexts.english: "Yes. If you truly desire it, you will indeed return to the same dream. I have experienced it myself."

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page101:1
contexts.japanese: そのような事はない。
contexts.english: It's not possible.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page101:1
contexts.japanese: 夢とは元々、一度きりで連続しないものを言う。
contexts.english: A dream is a fleeting thing...not something to return to.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page101:1
contexts.japanese: それでも騎士は偽った。
contexts.english: Even so, the knight lies to his king.

counterexamples.description: The king avoids looking up and issues the final order to take the sword.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The weakened voice and command remain distinct.
counterexamples.explanation: The king avoids looking up and issues the final order to take the sword.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page102:1
contexts.japanese: その顔は伏せたままで、騎士を見上げる事もしない。
contexts.english: The king's head remains tilted down, not looking up at the knight.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page102:1
contexts.japanese: 「ベディヴィエール。我が名剣をもて」
contexts.english: "Bedivere. Take my sword."

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page102:1
contexts.japanese: 掠れた声で、最後の命を口にした。
contexts.english: The knight receives his king's final order.

counterexamples.description: Returning the lake sword clearly means the end of the king.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Bedivere understands the sword's protective and royal-sign function.
counterexamples.explanation: Returning the lake sword clearly means the end of the king.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page103:1
contexts.japanese: 「よいか。この森を抜け、あの血塗られた丘を越えるのだ。その先には深い湖がある。そこに、我が剣を投げ入れよ」
contexts.english: "Listen. Pass through the forest and travel over that bloody hill. Beyond that, you will find a lake. Throw my sword into it."

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page103:1
contexts.japanese: それがどういう事なのか、騎士には判っていた。
contexts.english: The knight knows what that means.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page103:1
contexts.japanese: 湖の剣。
contexts.english: The sword in the lake.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page103:1
contexts.japanese: 今まで王を守り、王の証であった剣を手放すという事は、彼が仕えた王の終わりを意味するのだから。
contexts.english: To relinquish the sword that had protected the king and served as proof of kingship...would mean the end of his king.

counterexamples.description: Bedivere hesitates three times, disobeys twice, and finally returns the sword on the third visit.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The repetition is deliberate and does not need arithmetic correction.
counterexamples.explanation: Bedivere hesitates three times, disobeys twice, and finally returns the sword on the third visit.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page105:1
contexts.japanese: 騎士は三度に渡り、剣の返還を躊躇った。
contexts.english: Three times, the knight hesitates to follow his king's command.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page105:1
contexts.japanese: だが剣を投げ入れる事ができなかった。
contexts.english: But he cannot throw the sword away.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page105:1
contexts.japanese: 騎士は王を惜しむあまり剣を捨てられず、踵を返し、王の元へと立ち帰る。
contexts.english: The knight's unwillingness to part with his king stays his hand, and so he returns to his king.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page106:1
contexts.japanese: 王の命を破る、という事は騎士にとっては大罪に等しい。
contexts.english: To defy the king's order is a great sin for a knight.

contexts.ref: セイバーエピローグ:page106:1

counterexamples.explanation: After dinner Shirou cools his head until Saber reminds him of Rin's night lesson, and he goes to the upstairs guest room.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page0:1
contexts.japanese: —夕食が終わった。
contexts.english: We finish dinner.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page1:1
contexts.english: "...So cold."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page1:1
contexts.japanese: 縁側の窓を開け、外の風で頭を冷やしていたがそれもここまでだ。
contexts.english: I had opened a window from the veranda to let the outside wind cool my head, but I need to stop.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page1:1
contexts.japanese: いつまでもこんなコトしていたら風邪を引いちまう。
contexts.english: I'm going to catch a cold if I keep this up.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page2:1
contexts.japanese: 「シロウ、ここにいたのですか」
contexts.english: "Shirou, there you are."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page2:1
contexts.japanese: 「セ、セイバー……！？　な、なんだよ、俺になんか用か」
contexts.english: "S-Saber!? D-did you have something?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page3:1
contexts.english: "Oh."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page3:1
contexts.japanese: ぱし、と頭を叩く。
contexts.english: I smack my forehead.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page3:1
contexts.japanese: 「すっかり忘れてた。さんきゅ、今すぐ行ってくる！」
contexts.english: "I completely forgot. Thanks. I'll head over there right away!"

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page4:1
contexts.japanese: 別棟に駆け込んで、二階にあがる。
contexts.english: I rush to the outbuilding and head upstairs.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page4:1
contexts.japanese: 遠坂が占拠した客間のドアをノックすると、
contexts.english: I knock on the door to the guestroom that Tohsaka has taken up occupancy in.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page4:1
contexts.japanese: 「士郎？　いいわよ、ちょっと今手が放せないから、勝手に入って」
contexts.english: "Shirou? I have my hands full, so just come on in, it's fine."

counterexamples.description: Rin adapts the treatment and explicitly offers to stop if Shirou refuses.
counterexamples.sourceReading: No procedure is performed tonight and the commented switch explanation remains absent.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin adapts the treatment and explicitly offers to stop if Shirou refuses.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page61:1
contexts.japanese: 「さて、魔術を教えるって事だったけど、ちょっと予定が変わったわ。士郎に魔術刻印がないんなら違った方針を立てないといけないし。
contexts.english: "Well, I was supposed to teach you magecraft, but we got a little sidetracked. I'll need to come up with a different approach now that I know you don't have a Magic Crest.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page61:1
contexts.japanese: ……うん、今夜はここでお開きにしましょ。明日までには色々と用意しておくから、それまで待ってちょうだい」
contexts.english: Let's call it a night for now. I'll prepare some things for you tomorrow, so we'll do more then."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page62:1
contexts.japanese: 「？　遠坂がそう言うんなら頷くしかないんだが……なんだよ、その色々用意しておくって」
contexts.english: "Oh? I'll just have to trust you then...and what do you mean, you're going to prepare things?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page63:1
contexts.japanese: 「だから色々よ。刻印がないって事は、貴方スイッチできないんでしょ？　体の中身をいじるんだから、お薬とか矯正器具とか必要じゃない」
contexts.english: "I mean a lot of things. Since you have no crest, you don't have a switch. I'm going to go in and tamper with your body, so we'll need medicine and other tools."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page64:1
contexts.japanese: うわ。なんか、いま本気でぶるっときたんだがっ。
contexts.english: A chill runs down my spine.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page65:1
contexts.japanese: 「なに？　イヤだって言うんなら止めるけど。その場合、わたしが教えてあげられる事はなくなるわよ？」
contexts.english: "What? I'll stop if you don't want to do it. But if so, there won't be much I can teach you."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page65:1
contexts.japanese: 「あ……いや、イヤだけど、頼む。遠坂の言い分は、たぶん正しい」
contexts.english: "Uh...well I don't want to, but I'm still going to ask you. Whatever you say is probably the right way to go."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page67:1
contexts.japanese: 「じゃあ明日はそれで決まりね。
contexts.english: "Then that's what we'll do tomorrow.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page67:1
contexts.japanese: ……と、そうだ。貴方、明日もセイバーと剣の鍛錬をするつもり？」
contexts.english: Oh, right... Are you planning on training with Saber tomorrow too?"

counterexamples.description: Shirou continues training under his belief that the school field has not yet activated; Rin notices dinner silence and worries about combat cooperation.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou firmly trusts Saber as an ally while remaining uncertain about other feelings.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou continues training under his belief that the school field has not yet activated; Rin notices dinner silence and worries about combat cooperation.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page68:1
contexts.japanese: 「？　ああ、そうだけど。学校の結界も気がかりだけど、発動するまでまだ時間がある。それまで少しは戦えるようになっていたいんだ」
contexts.english: "Huh? Well, yeah. I'm concerned about the Bounded Field over the school, but there's still some time before it activates. I want to at least be able to fight by then."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page69:1
contexts.japanese: 「そ。まあいいけど。その割にはセイバーとはうまくいってないようじゃない？」
contexts.english: "I see. Well, not that it's important to me, but it seems like you and Saber aren't getting along."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page69:1
contexts.japanese: 「うっ……それは、その」
contexts.english: "Ugh...well, that..."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page70:1
contexts.japanese: 「夕食前までは普通に話せてたのに、夕食から妙に黙り込んでたし。
contexts.english: "You managed to talk normally before dinner, but you got all quiet at dinner.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page70:1
contexts.japanese: 念の為に聞くけど、貴方たちうまくいってるんでしょうね？　いざ戦闘って時に仲違いされたら、わたしたちまで被害を受けるんだから」
contexts.english: I just want to check: Are you two getting along? If you two end up bickering during battle, I'm going to suffer the consequences too, you know?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page71:1
contexts.english: Ugh...

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page71:1
contexts.japanese: それは単に、夕食前にトラブルがあっただけで、今はただ気まずいだけだ。
contexts.english: It's just that something happened right before dinner, and now things are awkward.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page71:1
contexts.japanese: だけなのだが……本当に、俺とセイバーはうまくいってるんだろうか？
contexts.english: That's all...but I'm not sure if Saber and I are really getting along.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page71:1
contexts.japanese: そりゃあ今日一日打ち合って、セイバーがどんなヤツかは少しは判ったとは思う。
contexts.english: When I spent all day dueling her, I think I got a sense of what Saber is like.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page72:1
contexts.japanese: 協力者として、セイバーは信頼できる。
contexts.english: I trust Saber as an ally.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page72:1
contexts.japanese: それは絶対だ。
contexts.english: No question about that.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page72:1
contexts.japanese: ただそれ以外の部分でセイバーをどう思っているかと言われると、返答に困ってしまう。
contexts.english: But if someone asked me how I feel about Saber in other senses, I wouldn't know how to answer.

counterexamples.description: Rin states that she likes Saber's strength, courtesy and beauty; Shirou's direct repetition embarrasses her, then his liking for Rin's manner produces another misread reaction.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Neither side explicitly recognizes a mutual romantic confession.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin states that she likes Saber's strength, courtesy and beauty; Shirou's direct repetition embarrasses her, then his liking for Rin's manner produces another misread reaction.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page73:1
contexts.japanese: 「……難しいな。そう言う遠坂はどうなんだよ。セイバーの事、好きなのか」
contexts.english: "It's hard to say. But what about you, Tohsaka? Do you like Saber?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page74:1
contexts.japanese: 「好きよ。だって嫌いになる要素がないじゃない。
contexts.english: "I do. There's nothing about her I don't like really.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page74:1
contexts.japanese: 強いし、礼儀正しいし、綺麗だし。うちの皮肉屋とは大違いだわ」
contexts.english: She's strong, polite, and pretty. A huge difference from my Mister Cynic."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page74:1
contexts.japanese: 「ふーん。そうか、遠坂はセイバーが好きなのか」
contexts.english: "Huh. I see. So you like Saber."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page75:1
contexts.japanese: 「っ—！　なによ、素直に好きな部類だって言っただけでしょ。あ、貴方ね、そのストレートな物言いは直しなさい。いろいろ敵を作りやすいから」
contexts.english: "What!? All I said was I like more about her than I don't! Quit being so blunt, or you'll make enemies!"

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page76:1
contexts.japanese: 「お断りだ。もともと口べたなんだよ、俺は」
contexts.english: "I refuse. I've never been good with words anyway."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page77:1
contexts.japanese: 「……そうでしょうよ。嫌味とか皮肉とか口にしなさそうだものね、士郎は。ええ、どうせわたしのコトなんて口うるさい嫌味なヤツだとか思ってるでしょ」
contexts.english: "I figured as much. You're never sarcastic or cynical. I bet you think of me as loud and annoying."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page78:1
contexts.japanese: 「？　なんでさ。俺、遠坂が言う分には好きだぞ。なんかさ、そうじゃないと遠坂じゃない気がするし」
contexts.english: "Why would I think that? I like the way you say things. Otherwise it wouldn't feel like it's really coming from you."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page78:1
contexts.english: "WHAT!?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page78:1
contexts.japanese: あ。
contexts.english: Crap.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page78:1
contexts.japanese: 癇に障ったのか、遠坂は不機嫌そうに顔を逸らしてしまった。
contexts.english: I might have struck a nerve. Tohsaka turns away, pouting.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-01:page79:1
contexts.japanese: まあ、それより今は、遠坂がセイバーを好きだと言ってくれたコトが、なんとなく嬉しかった。
contexts.english: But I have to admit, I feel a little better—even happy—knowing that Tohsaka likes Saber.

counterexamples.description: Shirou cleans the dojo out of respect, distinguishes repair interests from combat and recognizes this as his first serious sword instruction.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Prior shinai play does not make him a kendo expert.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou cleans the dojo out of respect, distinguishes repair interests from combat and recognizes this as his first serious sword instruction.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page0:1
contexts.japanese: 「さて、雑巾がけぐらいしとかないとな」
contexts.english: "I should probably clean the floors."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page0:1
contexts.japanese: セイバーには少ししてから来るように伝えてある。
contexts.english: I told Saber to meet me here a little later.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page0:1
contexts.japanese: いつも最低限の掃除はしているが、こうして誰かと手合わせするのは何年かぶりだ。
contexts.english: I always just do the bare minimum of cleaning in here. It's been years since I sparred with anyone in this place.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page0:1
contexts.japanese: 雑巾がけの一つもしておかないと道場にもセイバーにも失礼だろう。
contexts.english: It'd probably be rude to both the dojo and Saber if I don't clean up a little.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page1:1
contexts.japanese: 「……しっかしあれだな。剣の修行って言っても何をやらされるのやら」
contexts.english: "But honestly, I don't know what she's going to do for sword training."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page3:1
contexts.japanese: 「……そもそも道具を使ってケンカするのは苦手だったな。作ったり直したりする方にしか関心がないんだから」
contexts.english: "I was never keen on using tools in a fight. My interest was always making and fixing them."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page4:1
contexts.japanese: そういった意味で言えば、まともに剣というものを教わるのは初めてだ。
contexts.english: In that sense, this might be the first time for me to learn proper swordsmanship in any serious sense.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page4:1
contexts.japanese: セイバーの剣は剣道とは大きく違うようだが、それでも通じるところはありそうだし、ついていけなくなるほど突拍子もない物じゃないだろう。
contexts.english: Saber's swordsmanship is different than kendo, but I'm sure there are some things in common, and I don't think they're so different I won't be able to keep up.

counterexamples.description: Shirou's aesthetic preference for Saber's ordinary clothes and Saber's functional warrior assessment talk past each other.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Saber does not actually change into armor.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's aesthetic preference for Saber's ordinary clothes and Saber's functional warrior assessment talk past each other.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page6:1
contexts.japanese: 「待たせたな。今日からここで手ほどきをしてもらう訳だけど—」
contexts.english: "Sorry I made you wait. I was thinking of having you teach me here..."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page6:1
contexts.japanese: 「？　どうかしましたかシロウ。何か意外なものを見るような顔をしていますが」
contexts.english: "Yes? Is something the matter, Shirou? You look like you have just seen something unusual."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page7:1
contexts.japanese: 「あ—いや、セイバーの服がそのままだったから、驚いた。てっきりあっちの格好で来るのかと思ってたから」
contexts.english: "Oh...it's nothing. I was just surprised that you're still in the same clothes. I thought you were going to wear your other outfit."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page8:1
contexts.japanese: 「はあ。武装している方がいい、というのでしたら着替えますが。……そうですね、私がどうかしていました。
contexts.english: "Huh. If you prefer me armored, I can change. You are right...I was not thinking.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page8:1
contexts.japanese: たとえ試合とは言え、鎧をまとわないのはシロウに失礼です。申し訳ありません、すぐに着替えてきます」
contexts.english: Even should we only be practicing, I am disrespecting you by not wearing my armor. My apologies. I will change right away."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page9:1
contexts.japanese: 「あ—いや、別にそういう訳じゃない。ただの思い違いだからいいんだ。俺もどっちかっていうと、鎧姿より今の方がいい」
contexts.english: "Oh...uh, that's not what I mean. I just misunderstood. It's fine. I actually prefer you in this outfit to your armor."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page10:1
contexts.japanese: 「は……？　ですが、この服装ではシロウの気が済まないのではないのですか？」
contexts.english: "Huh? Are you not saying my outfit is unsatisfactory?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page10:1
contexts.japanese: 「気が済まないって……確かに今から試合するぞー、って感じじゃないけど、セイバーが動きやすいっていうんなら問題ないだろ。昼間っから鎧を着込んでたら、セイバーだって疲れるしな」
contexts.english: "Unsatisfactory? I mean, you don't look like you're dressed for a bout right now, but it shouldn't matter as long as you're comfortable. Wearing armor all day will just tire you out."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page11:1
contexts.japanese: 「それはそうですが—この服装で剣を振るうのはおかしくはないでしょうか？」
contexts.english: "That may be true...but don't you think this is an inappropriate look for wielding a sword?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page11:1
contexts.japanese: 「なんでさ。似合ってるんだからおかしくなんかないぞ。
contexts.english: "Why would you think that? It's not weird; you look good.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page11:1
contexts.japanese: 俺、セイバーは鎧姿より今の方がいいと思う」
contexts.english: I think you look better right now than you do in your armor."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page12:1
contexts.japanese: 「……？　理解しかねます。この服装は確かに気軽なのですが、戦闘には耐えられないでしょう。セイバーとしては不向きな姿だと思うのですが」
contexts.english: "I do not quite understand. This outfit is certainly easy to move in, but it is ill-suited for combat. I believe this is quite an inadequate look for a Saber."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page12:1
contexts.japanese: 「その格好で戦うな、ばか。セイバーは女の子だろ。女の子にはそういう服のが似合うんだから、それでいいんだ」
contexts.english: "Don't you dare wear that outfit in a fight, dummy. You're a girl, Saber. Girls look good in outfits like this, so this is fine."

counterexamples.description: Saber's distraction leads Shirou to imagine wooden or real blades, but she accepts the shinai as excellent practice weapons.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Five hundred swings and running remain questions, not completed tasks.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber's distraction leads Shirou to imagine wooden or real blades, but she accepts the shinai as excellent practice weapons.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page13:1
contexts.japanese: さて。
contexts.english: And then...

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page13:1
contexts.japanese: 使っていた雑巾をバケツに戻して、壁際にある竹刀を二本持ってくる。
contexts.english: I return the rag I'd been cleaning with to the bucket, and I bring back two shinai that had been leaning against a wall.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page14:1
contexts.japanese: 「さて。それでどういった鍛錬をするんだセイバー。方針は全部セイバーに任せるから、無茶でもなんでも言ってくれ」
contexts.english: "So what are you planning for training, Saber? I'm leaving everything to you to decide, so tell me anything, no matter how absurd it might be."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page14:1
contexts.japanese: 竹刀をセイバーに投げる。
contexts.english: I toss her the bamboo sword.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page15:1
contexts.japanese: セイバーは心ここにあらず、といった体で竹刀を受け取って、まじまじとこちらを見つめていた。
contexts.english: Saber seems distracted as she catches the shinai and stares at me quietly.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page16:1
contexts.japanese: 「？　なんだよ、竹刀じゃダメか？
contexts.english: "Huh? Is there a problem with bamboo swords?

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page16:1
contexts.japanese: ま、まさか木刀—いや真剣を使えってんじゃないだろうな！」
contexts.english: D-don't tell me you want to use wooden—or even real blades!?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page16:1
contexts.japanese: なんてスパルタ！　そりゃ流石に想像以上だ。
contexts.english: She's really a tough instructor! This is beyond anything I imagined!

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page17:1
contexts.japanese: 「ぁ—いえ、そのような事はありません。せっかく優れた試合用の模造刀があるのですから、こちらを使う事にしましょう」
contexts.english: "Oh...no, that is not it. These are certainly excellent mock swords for practice sessions, so let us use them."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page17:1
contexts.japanese: すう、と何やら静かに深呼吸をするセイバー。
contexts.english: Saber draws in a deep breath...

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page17:1
contexts.japanese: それきり、彼女はいつものセイバーに戻っていた。
contexts.english: ...and goes right back to being the normal Saber as I know her.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page18:1
contexts.japanese: ……で、ほんとに何をやればいいんだ？　まず素振り五百回とか、走り込みとか、そういう体力作りからか？」
contexts.english: So, what are we going to do? Are you going to make me strengthen my body by swinging the sword five hundred times or run laps?"

counterexamples.description: Saber judges bodily conditioning adequate but insufficient against Servants and chooses repeated lethal-intent bouts because technique cannot be taught overnight.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She does not offer a winning trick.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber judges bodily conditioning adequate but insufficient against Servants and chooses repeated lethal-intent bouts because technique cannot be taught overnight.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page19:1
contexts.japanese: 「その必要はないでしょう。私から見ても、シロウの運動能力は水準に達しています。これ以上肉体面を鍛えるのであれば、それは一日や二日で出来る事ではありません」
contexts.english: "That will not be necessary. From what I've observed, your athletic abilities are above average. If we intended to further fortify your body, it would take more than a day or two."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page20:1
contexts.japanese: 「シロウは魔術師としては未熟ですが、戦士としては悲観したものではないと思います。幼い頃から、よほど懸命に鍛えてきたのですね」
contexts.english: "You may be unskilled as a mage, but you are not bad as a warrior. You must have trained hard from a young age."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page20:1
contexts.japanese: 「う—まあ、それぐらいしか取り柄がなかったからな。体を鍛えるのだけは、魔術の才能がなくても出来た事だし」
contexts.english: "Uh...well, that's all I was really good at. You don't have to be talented in magecraft to work out physically."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page21:1
contexts.japanese: 「それが幸いしたのでしょう。ランサーに襲われて死に至らなかったのは、シロウのそういう努力のたまものですから」
contexts.english: "That must have worked in your favor. One of the reasons you survived Lancer's attack must be that very training."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page22:1
contexts.japanese: 人間には限界がある。シロウの体はその限界の域にはほど遠いし、突破する事も難しいでしょう。
contexts.english: Humans are bound by limitations. Your body has not yet reached its limit, and breaking through that limit would be difficult.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page23:1
contexts.japanese: 「……？　戦う事だけってどういう事だ。今の口振りからして、戦う方法を教えてくれる……って訳じゃなさそうだけど」
contexts.english: "What do you mean, just fight? Based on your tone, it doesn't sound like you'll teach me how to fight."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page24:1
contexts.japanese: 「当然です。一朝一夕で戦闘技術など身に付く筈がないでしょう。私に出来る事は、マスターに一回でも多く戦いを味わってもらう事だけです。
contexts.english: "Of course not. The techniques employed in battle cannot be learned overnight. All I can do is make certain Master experiences as many battles as possible.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page24:1
contexts.japanese: そもそも人に物を教える事は苦手なのですから、私に師事されても困ります」
contexts.english: I am not a skilled teacher, so I am baffled that you would seek my guidance."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page25:1
contexts.japanese: 「—もしもし？」
contexts.english: "...Um, hello?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page25:1
contexts.japanese: そういう事を胸張って言われても、教え子としては答えに窮するというか。
contexts.english: Having her sound so proud about that makes it a bit awkward for me as her student.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page26:1
contexts.japanese: 「……えっと、つまり。ようするに、ただ試合をするだけってコトかな、セイバー」
contexts.english: "Uh...so, we're just going to have a bunch of matches?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page26:1
contexts.japanese: 「—ええ。ただそれだけです、マスター。
contexts.english: "Yes. That is all, Master.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page26:1
contexts.japanese: ……そうですね、一時間もすればどういう事なのか、理解してもらえると思います」
contexts.english: Well, you will understand after perhaps an hour."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page27:1
contexts.japanese: では、とセイバーは竹刀を軽く握り込む。
contexts.english: Saber readies herself, gently gripping her shinai.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page27:1
contexts.japanese: その言葉に首をかしげつつ、こちらもセイバーに倣って竹刀を握る。
contexts.english: I tilt my head, wondering what she means, but I also grip my shinai as Saber does.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page27:1
contexts.japanese: 途端。
contexts.english: In that instant...

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page27:1
contexts.japanese: ものの見事に、世界が暗転した。
contexts.english: My vision goes black.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page28:1
contexts.japanese: 要するに、セイバーが教えようとしているコトはただ一つ。
contexts.english: Saber is teaching me one very simple lesson:

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page28:1
contexts.japanese: どんなコトをやっても、
contexts.english: No matter what I do...

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page28:1
contexts.japanese: どんな奇策を用いても、
contexts.english: No matter what strategy I come up with...

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page28:1
contexts.japanese: 敵わないヤツには絶対に敵わない、という事実だけだった。
contexts.english: None of it will change the outcome of a fight against someone I just don't have a chance of beating.

counterexamples.description: A severe bruise prompts rest; Shirou tries one opportunistic attack, then accepts that conditions and retreat must be prepared before fighting a Servant.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Saber does not say the bruise is immediately safe for motion.
counterexamples.explanation: A severe bruise prompts rest; Shirou tries one opportunistic attack, then accepts that conditions and retreat must be prepared before fighting a Servant.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page29:1
contexts.japanese: 「—ぁ—はあ、はあ、はあ、あ—あいたたた、いたい、これホントに折れてるって、間違いなく……！」
contexts.english: "Haaa...haaah...ah...ha...haaa...ouch. That hurt! It's definitely broken!"

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page30:1
contexts.japanese: 「……つ、そうか。よし、なら、もう少し続けるか」
contexts.english: "...Tch. Okay. Then let's keep going."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page31:1
contexts.japanese: 「え……まだ続けるのですか、シロウ？
contexts.english: "Huh? Do you intend to continue, Shirou?

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page31:1
contexts.japanese: 確かに打ち身ではありますが、すぐに動いていいものではありません」
contexts.english: It may be a bruise, but you should not move again so quickly."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page32:1
contexts.japanese: —いいぜ、セイバーが乗り気じゃないんなら、その隙—」
contexts.english: Fine. If you don't feel like it, I'll use this opportunity—"

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page32:1
contexts.japanese: もらった！
contexts.english: I got her!

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page32:1
contexts.japanese: ……わけないよな、そりゃ。
contexts.english: ...Nope. Obviously.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page33:1
contexts.japanese: 「人の話を聞いてください。明らかにシロウは疲労しています。そんな体ではせっかくの修練も無駄になるのですから、休憩をいれるべきです」
contexts.english: "Please listen to me. You are obviously fatigued. You must rest, or all our training will be in vain."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page34:1
contexts.japanese: 「—いや、でもな。こう、明らかに手加減されてるのに打たれっぱなしっていうのは情けない。
contexts.english: "But it's disgraceful for you to beat me so badly when you're so obviously taking it easy on me!

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page34:1
contexts.japanese: せめて一太刀、セイバーの眉ぐらいは動かさなきゃ悔しくて倒れられん」
contexts.english: If I can't even get you to so much as raise a brow, I'll be too frustrated to even collapse!"

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page35:1
contexts.japanese: 「驚くというのでしたら、もう十分驚いています。強情だとは思っていましたが、まさかこれほどとは思っていなかった」
contexts.english: "If you want me to be surprised, I am plenty surprised. I knew you were stubborn, but I entirely failed to anticipate the extent."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page35:1
contexts.japanese: 「悪かったな。根本的に負けず嫌いなんだ、俺」
contexts.english: "Well sorry about that. I hate losing."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page36:1
contexts.japanese: 「ええ、それは嫌というほど思い知りましたので結構です。ともかく休憩にしますから、シロウも竹刀を置いてください。
contexts.english: "Yes. You have demonstrated that many times, so you needn't say so. We will be taking a break, so please put your bamboo sword down.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page36:1
contexts.japanese: 床も汗で滑りやすくなっている。極限状態での模擬戦でもなし、疲労困憊して足場も不確か—などという状態では意味がありません」
contexts.english: The floor is slippery with sweat. We are not trying to carry out mock battles in extreme situations, so there is no point in carrying on while we are exhausted and on unstable footing."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page37:1
contexts.japanese: 「……なんでさ。普通、戦闘訓練ってのは最悪の状態を想定してやるもんだろ。なら」
contexts.english: "Why not? I thought combat training was supposed to simulate worst-case scenarios. If not..."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page38:1
contexts.japanese: 「それこそ無意味です。
contexts.english: "That is even more pointless.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page38:1
contexts.japanese: いいですかシロウ。貴方がサーヴァントと戦う、というのでしたら、体力は万全、足場は完全、逃走経路は確保済み、という状況以外での戦闘は無意味です。
contexts.english: Listen, Shirou. If you say you are going to fight against a Servant, doing so will be pointless unless you are in peak condition, have the best footing, and a prepared path of retreat.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page39:1
contexts.japanese: 「……う。つまりこういう状態では、間違っても戦うなってコトか」
contexts.english: "Ungh...so what you're saying is that I shouldn't even bother trying to fight in situations like this."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page39:1
contexts.japanese: 「そういうコトです。そうなってはどのような奇蹟もシロウを救いはしないでしょう。
contexts.english: "Exactly. In a situation like this, there is no miracle which would save you, Shirou.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page40:1
contexts.japanese: 「…………納得。それじゃ、申し訳ないけど、休ませてくれ」
contexts.english: "...Got it. Then I'd like to take a break."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page40:1
contexts.japanese: ばたん、と壁にもたれかかって、そのままずるずると腰を下ろす。
contexts.english: I slump against the wall and slowly slide down to the floor.

counterexamples.description: From nine to after eleven Shirou repeatedly blacks out, learns to receive an opening blow and develops danger intuition without landing a successful counterattack.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Fatality language remains experiential metaphor within repeated training.
counterexamples.explanation: From nine to after eleven Shirou repeatedly blacks out, learns to receive an opening blow and develops danger intuition without landing a successful counterattack.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page42:1
contexts.english: "...Ouch."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page42:1
contexts.japanese: 体中がズキズキと痛む中、ちらりと壁の時計を見る。
contexts.english: While my body is throbbing with pain, I glance towards the clock on the wall.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page42:1
contexts.japanese: 時刻は十一時過ぎ。
contexts.english: It's a little past eleven o'clock.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page42:1
contexts.japanese: はじめたのが九時頃だから、都合二時間打ち合っていた訳か。
contexts.english: We started around nine, so we've been sparring for about two hours.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page43:1
contexts.japanese: 初めの一時間は、一方的に叩かれただけだった。
contexts.english: During the first hour, I was just getting beaten up.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page43:1
contexts.japanese: いきなりセイバーの一撃がとんできて、軽い失神。
contexts.english: Saber struck suddenly, then I blacked out.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page43:1
contexts.japanese: 目が覚めて、次は気を付けるぞと思った矢先に失神。
contexts.english: I woke up, thinking I would be more careful, and then just got knocked right back out.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page43:1
contexts.japanese: ともかく何度も何度も打ちのめされ、体の方が慣れたのか、怒りで馬鹿力が出たのか、一撃目はなんとか受けられるようになった。
contexts.english: After getting beaten up repeatedly, my body seemed to get used to it, or maybe my anger just triggered some latent power, but eventually I did manage to block the first blow.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page44:1
contexts.japanese: 問題はその後。
contexts.english: The problem came after that.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page44:1
contexts.japanese: さて、それだけの戦力差を見せつけられて、人間ってのはおいそれと襲いかかれるものなのか。
contexts.english: Here's a thought: Would humans dare to, or even be able to fight back against an opponent who is so much stronger and more skilled?

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page45:1
contexts.english: "...You oni."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page45:1
contexts.japanese: 正解は、ひるんだ瞬間に失神だった。
contexts.english: The answer was no, because I blacked out the instant I flinched.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page46:1
contexts.japanese: どう防いでも致命傷を食らって倒れるなら、もう自棄になって攻め込むしかない。
contexts.english: If, no matter how I tried to block the attack, I was just going to fall, mortally wounded, then I had no choice but to attack in desperation.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page46:1
contexts.japanese: そんなものは当然のようにあしらわれてまた倒される訳だが、それに慣れてくると、なんていうか、
contexts.english: Of course, she deflected my attacks easily and knocked me out. But as I got used to it...

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page46:1
contexts.japanese: こういうのを、俗に乗ってきた、という。
contexts.english: I guess in a general sense, I was getting into the swing of things.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page47:1
contexts.japanese: そうなると、後は必死に受けに回った。
contexts.english: So after that, I went on the defensive.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page47:1
contexts.japanese: とにかく、アレを食らったら失神する、なんて直感がビシバシ来るわけで、生き物としちゃそんなのは避けるのが道理。
contexts.english: My intuition kept screaming that the next attack would knock me out, so I tried to avoid it, like any living thing would.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page48:1
contexts.japanese: 雨のように繰り出されるセイバーの竹刀をなんとか受け流して、反撃の隙をじっと待っているうちに致命傷を食らってしまう。
contexts.english: I managed to parry Saber's shinai attacks as they rained down upon me, and while I waited for an opening to counterattack, she struck a fatal blow.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page48:1
contexts.japanese: で、立ち上がって次はなんとかもうちょっと持ち堪えるか、いやいやどうせ持ち堪えられないんだからやられる前にやれ、とばかりに攻め込んだりもする。
contexts.english: I managed to stand up and think that next time I'd last longer, then think maybe I should just go on the offensive before she can strike, since I couldn't hold out anyway.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page49:1
contexts.japanese: この二時間は、その繰り返しだった。
contexts.english: And that went on for two hours.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page49:1
contexts.japanese: ……こんな事をして強くなれるかなんて判らない。
contexts.english: ...I'm not sure this is going to make me stronger.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page49:1
contexts.japanese: これはただ、戦いっていうものに慣れさせるだけの打ち合いにすぎないと思う。
contexts.english: But I do think it's helping me get used to fighting.

counterexamples.description: The training builds life-or-death tension rather than technical victory; Shirou admits pure sour grapes and Saber distinguishes adjustment from mercy.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She neither fights at full Servant power nor treats him gently.
counterexamples.explanation: The training builds life-or-death tension rather than technical victory; Shirou admits pure sour grapes and Saber distinguishes adjustment from mercy.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page50:1
contexts.japanese: 敵を目の前にしても混乱せず、かといって冷静すぎず。
contexts.english: Practice so I'm neither confused nor too calm in the face of the enemy.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page51:1
contexts.japanese: それでも—それは無意味かと言われると、そうでもない。
contexts.english: But...if you asked me if I thought this was meaningless, I'd say no.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page51:1
contexts.japanese: なんの武器もない自分にとって、この緊張感こそが、最も大事にしなければならないモノだと思うのだ。
contexts.english: With no effective weapon to use, the feeling of constantly being on edge is the most important thing I have.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page52:1
contexts.japanese: 「お疲れさまでした。どこか痛むところはありますか、シロウ」
contexts.english: "A job well done. Are you hurt anywhere, Shirou?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page53:1
contexts.japanese: 気が付けば、傍らにはセイバーがやってきていた。
contexts.english: The next thing I know, Saber is right next to me.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page54:1
contexts.japanese: 「痛まないところのが珍しいぐらいだ。
contexts.english: "It'd be hard to find anywhere that doesn't hurt at this point.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page54:1
contexts.japanese: 白状しよう。１００％負け惜しみである。
contexts.english: I have to admit, I'm saying that entirely because I'm a sore loser.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page55:1
contexts.japanese: 「はい。シロウに合わせて加減はしましたが、容赦はしないよう心がけました。手心を加えては戦いにはなりませんから」
contexts.english: "Yes. I did try to bring myself down to your level, but I also tried to show you no mercy. No real battle will ever involve making things easy for you."

counterexamples.description: Saber's praise restores Shirou's awareness of gender; she fetches water, then he admires her as a beautiful human while alone with her.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The moment retains both embarrassment and his explicit nonsexual self-description.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber's praise restores Shirou's awareness of gender; she fetches water, then he admires her as a beautiful human while alone with her.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page57:1
contexts.japanese: 素直に反省。
contexts.english: I'm in a moment of honest reflection.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page58:1
contexts.japanese: 「いいえ、そのような事はありません。シロウの打ち込みは一心で、力がありました。時に、あまりの熱心さに対応を忘れたほどです」
contexts.english: "That is not true. Your attacks were all quite powerful. I was so enthused by your efforts that I forgot to strike back at times."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page59:1
contexts.english: "Oh?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page59:1
contexts.japanese: 途端、気恥ずかしさが戻ってくる。
contexts.english: I'm suddenly embarrassed again.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page59:1
contexts.japanese: 今までは竹刀をもった同士、男も女もなく打ち合っていたけど、これはその—不意打ち、ではないか。
contexts.english: For a while, we'd just been two people sparring with our shinai with no thought given to being a man and a woman, but now...she's caught me off guard.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page60:1
contexts.japanese: 「いや、ちょっと待った。水飲んでくる、俺」
contexts.english: "Uh...hold on. I'm going to go drink some water."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page60:1
contexts.japanese: 「水ですか？　それでしたら私が汲んできますから、シロウは休んでいてください」
contexts.english: "Water? I will fetch you some. Please stay here and rest."

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page60:1
contexts.japanese: セイバーは水を汲みにいってくれた。
contexts.english: Saber goes to get some water.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page62:1
contexts.japanese: セイバーが汲んできてくれた水を飲む。
contexts.english: I drink the water Saber brings me.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page63:1
contexts.japanese: ……ああしているセイバーは、本当に綺麗だと思う。
contexts.english: Saber is so beautiful when she does that kind of thing.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page63:1
contexts.japanese: 男として異性を美しい、と感じるのではなく、人間として綺麗と思うのだ。
contexts.english: I'm not saying that as a man finding a woman attractive, but because I find her beautiful as a human being.

contexts.ref: セイバールート七日目-02:page65:1
contexts.japanese: 今、ここには自分とセイバーしかいない。
contexts.english: Right now, there's only me and Saber.

counterexamples.description: Saber’s responsibility, uncertainty, and desire to try again remain separate.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Saber gives responsibility as her answer, then qualifies her self-understanding and says she may merely want to do things over.
